what: Supervised one-off: real https://www.amazon.com/s?k=stag+fellow+kettle+base in Playwright WebKit 1.64.1 (webkit-2370), 1280x900, engine at HEAD 8ecdafb injected like the e2e harness (mode always), 20 scroll steps of 600px every 250ms. MutationObserver callbacks wrapped to time them (page's and engine's).
reading: Engine adds ~270 ms of MutationObserver work during load+scroll (35x baseline), a single 73 ms callback, and a 169 ms worst frame (vs 58). The page has 53 sheets but only 470 CSSOM-readable rules: most are cross-origin, so the engine re-fetches them and emits ~3,700 override rules, and every DOM mutation batch appears to trigger re-scans. Headless WebKit on an M-series Mac, so real Safari with an isolated-world content script will be worse, which matches the owner's 'very laggy'.
suspects_for_T013: re-scanning sheets or the whole subtree per mutation batch instead of only added nodes
regenerating or replacing the full override <style> on each change (forces full style recalc over 6.9k nodes)
no batching or idle scheduling (requestIdleCallback / chunking under 8 ms)
unbounded work on attribute mutations (Amazon flips class/style attributes constantly)
